title: The Contract Wife
excerpt: A marriage made on paper becomes dangerously real when the rules begin to change.

sections.title: The Agreement
paragraphs: At nine minutes past midnight, Mara signed her name beneath a line that turned a business arrangement into a marriage.
Across the polished table, Adrian Vale watched the ink dry. He looked exactly as he did in magazine photographs—calm, expensive, and impossible to read.
There were seven rules in the contract. No questions after midnight. No public arguments. No falling in love. Mara had laughed at the last one, because it seemed the easiest to keep.

sections.title: The First Rule
paragraphs: Three weeks later, the first rule broke on a rainy Thursday when Adrian came home bleeding from the hand and refused to explain why.
Mara found the first-aid kit without asking. He sat at the kitchen island while she wrapped his palm in gauze, both of them pretending the silence meant nothing.
When she finished, he did not let go immediately. That was when she began to understand that contracts could describe behavior, but never contain it.

sections.title: What Wasn't Written
paragraphs: By winter, their staged photographs no longer felt staged. Adrian remembered how she took her coffee. Mara knew which meetings left him restless enough to pace the hallway at two in the morning.
Neither of them mentioned rule seven. It remained on paper, untouched and increasingly absurd.
On the final day of the contract, Adrian placed the unsigned renewal in front of her. Beside it was a second sheet with only one sentence: Stay because you want to.
